name: Color Palette Discipline
summary: A single page should use ~6–8 distinct colors total; every additional hue dilutes hierarchy and signals nothing new.
description: Color is a signal. When a page contains 10+ distinct hexes, the eye can no longer tell which colors mean something (brand, action, error) and which are incidental. A disciplined palette is roughly: 1 primary brand color, 1 accent for CTAs and emphasis, 3–4 neutrals (text, muted text, border, background, surface), and 1–2 semantic colors (success, error/warning). Hover, active, and decorative variants should be derived from this small set via opacity or HSL adjustments — not introduced as new hexes. Near-duplicate values (#333 vs #363636) still count against the budget because they add cognitive noise without adding meaning. The discipline isn't aesthetic minimalism; it's making sure every color the user sees is doing a job.
implications: Define a token set of 6–8 base colors before generating any UI, and reuse them everywhere
Derive hover/active/disabled states with opacity (e.g., 0.8, 0.6) or lightness shifts from existing tokens, not new hexes
Express shadows as rgba() from a neutral token, not as standalone hex colors
Treat gradient stops as variations of existing tokens, not as license to add new hues
Audit generated pages by counting distinct hex values — flag anything over ~10
Collapse near-duplicate hexes (within ~5% lightness) into a single token
violations: A landing page with 11+ distinct hex values where several are visually indistinguishable
Introducing a new gray (#363636) when #333 is already in the palette
Hardcoding hover states as new hexes instead of deriving them from the base token
Decorative tints and gradient stops that don't map to any defined token
Shadow colors written as opaque hex values rather than rgba from a neutral
sources: Complements color-theory principles (which colors work together) with a constraint on how many should appear at once.
Raven self-audit (2026-06-14): 5 generated demos each landed at 11 distinct hexes, exceeding the ~10-color hierarchy threshold.
